output.narrative_summary: This result rests on the link from Engineering Capacity to Total Cost of Ownership, which is not yet well evidenced. If capacity assumptions change, more runs could support a different option. In this model, 58% of runs supported Rebuild In House.

story_headlines.opt_rebuild: Rebuild In House gains when engineering capacity holds up as modelled, lowering total cost of ownership.
story_headlines.opt_extend: Extend Vendor Contract gains more runs if vendor price path stays flatter than currently modelled.

robustness_explanation.summary: The ordering holds in about 61% of variations, based on current estimates given the low overall confidence behind this comparison.
robustness_explanation.primary_risk: The link from Engineering Capacity to Total Cost of Ownership is not well evidenced and could shift the comparison.
fragility_factors: The link from Engineering Capacity to Total Cost of Ownership is the main source of fragility in this result.

output.readiness_rationale: Two gaps still hold this back: engineering capacity is asserted rather than evidenced, and confidence behind both factors remains low. More evidence would settle this further.

fac_eng_capacity.specific_action: Run a capacity audit against current engineering headcount and planned commitments to test the assumption directly.
fac_eng_capacity.rationale: This factor carries the most value-of-information in this comparison and is currently asserted rather than evidenced.
